lessons.story:
In a classroom activity, students put ten bean seeds on wet paper in each of two trays. They place one tray on a shelf near the window and the other inside a dark cupboard. Both places feel equally warm.

Every morning, they add the same amount of water and count new roots. After three days, eight seeds in each tray have roots. Mei is surprised because she expected the dark tray to remain empty.

The teacher asks the class to record what they actually see. These seeds began growing in both places. That observation does not show that light never matters. The class has only watched the first few days.

For the next week, they will measure the young plants and note changes in their leaves. They keep the water schedule unchanged so they can compare the trays more carefully.
lessons.title: Seeds on Two Shelves
